title: Common gate
description: A common-gate stage: the input drives the source, the gate is AC-grounded, and the output is taken at the drain. It presents a low input resistance $R_{in} = 1/g_m$ (a current-mode input, so it is the classic input matching / current-buffer stage) and a non-inverting voltage gain $A_v = g_m*par(R_{load}, 1/g_{ds})$ equal in magnitude to a common source. Its current transfer from source to drain is essentially unity, so it passes an input current to the load with a low input impedance. The device source sits at the input DC level $V_{in}$, so the bind declares $V_{SB} = V_{in}$ (body grounded); on a table without a $V_{SB}$ axis this is advisory and the body effect $g_{mb}$ is omitted from $R_{in}$.

params.name: R_load
params.note: load resistor at the drain: sets the gain

params.name: cdd_est
params.note: output-node parasitic estimate; refine from extraction

params.name: gm_id
params.note: lower gm/ID raises gm, so it lowers Rin = 1/gm (better matching) at the cost of headroom

rows.name: Rin
rows.note: low-frequency input resistance looking into the source; gmb omitted (not on every table)

rows.name: Av
rows.note: non-inverting gain, gm into the load in parallel with the device output resistance

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: device channel thermal density; a common-gate input also passes the source's own noise, which is set outside this stage
